todays_decisions.reasoning: Agree with the Market Analyst's neutral stance: the trend is healthy (SPY 6.9% above its 200-day, calm vol) but growth is weak and this morning's futures are lower on Middle East escalation with Brent near $111. Cash is 47% of equity and the owner wants the account mostly invested within about a week, so I approve all four proposals but shrink each, staging the deployment (about $85 today) rather than going in at a risk-off open. Lessons L1 and L2 shaped the calls: all stops and invalidations are measured from the actual fill, and earnings dates for KR (12-03), MSCI (reported 10-20) and CARG (11-05) were checked against the news note. The Skeptic's staples-concentration objection on KR was the strongest point, so KR is cut the most. No earnings-window names were bought.

trades.thesis: Staples is a Market Analyst favored sector, KR has low event risk (next earnings 12-03, the 10-20 8-K was an investor-day update) and the sell side is supportive after the 7-11% EPS CAGR target. The Skeptic and Implicator are right that this stacks on WMT and DPZ (staples about 22.5% of equity) and that the negative beta is a statistical artifact, so I take a smaller position, which lifts staples only to about 25.9%.
trades.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price, or the 10-17 grocery-chain cyber incident is confirmed to be Kroger, or a guidance cut at the 12-03 print.

trades.thesis: Clean Q3 beat with the earnings event passed (the issue that sank it on 10-20), F-score 8, cfo $1.59B vs net income $1.20B, beta 0.34, and it adds a sector the book does not hold. The Skeptic is right that the sector label is Industrials (not a favored sector) and that the post-print re-rating is partly priced, so I trim the size and rest the case on quality and diversification only.
trades.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price (anchored to the fill, not the pre-print 563.49 close, per L1), or a guidance cut or negative 8-K follow-up.

trades.thesis: Broad-market exposure to deploy idle cash while the trend is intact and breadth is improving. Resulting US broad-ETF weight is about 18.4%.
trades.invalidation: SPY closes below its 200-day SMA (723.23), or the position is down more than 8% from the actual fill.

trades.thesis: Rank 2 on fundamentals (gross profitability 1.27, cfo about 2x net income), earnings 11-05 are outside the 5-day window, and no adverse headlines. The Skeptic's objections (averaging a one-day-old position, Technology label against the sector view, vol near the cutoff) justify a small add: the combined position is about 5%, and I will judge it as one position.
trades.invalidation: Combined position closes more than 10% below the average fill (measured from actual fills, per L1), or a negative earnings surprise appears inside the next five trading days.

DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes below $274.88 (10% under the $305.42 reference close), or a fundamentals screen (including one that reflects the Q3 results reported 10-13) drops it from the menu or shows cfo below net income.

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name in a favored sector (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.941, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, no added leverage or dilution). Sized down to $40 because its 0.814 beta (-$3.26 on this position in a 10% drop) makes it the least defensive holding in the book. Earnings are estimated for 11-02, outside the 5-day window.
IDXX.invalidation: IDXX closes below $500.22 (10% under the $555.80 reference close), or IDXX underperforms XLV by more than 5 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window.

VOO.thesis: Broad, diversified US core for idle cash while the long-term regime is on (SPY 6.1% above its 200-day, 63-day +2.69%), and the Market Analyst rates broad US equity acceptable at moderate size. This is a first lot below the $90 cap because of the mega-cap earnings week, the Iran/Hormuz tail risk and rate-hike odds; add the rest after those earnings if the regime holds.
VOO.invalidation: SPY closes below ~736.8 (within 2% of its 200-day SMA of 722.32), or HYG's 21-day return falls below -3% or HYG closes more than 3% below its 200-day.

WMT.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
WMT.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.

FAST.thesis: Lowest volatility on the menu (0.243), F-score 8/9, gross profitability at the 89th sector percentile, and operating cash flow above net income. It adds a first Consumer Discretionary exposure, not overlapping the staples names held. Resized from $40: the Skeptic is right that its earnings date was never verified, that cash conversion is only about 1.03x, and that the sector label may flatter it. The Implicator confirmed the diversification claim holds.
FAST.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an earnings report showing operating cash flow clearly below net income.

BTC/USD.thesis: A small crypto slot: trend still positive (63-day +28%, 14% above its 200-day), ETF inflows recovering, and no exchange failures or new adverse regulatory action. Resized from $20: the Skeptic is right that the thesis is mostly diversification, volatility is 44%, and the recovery partly rides on the same Iran-deal headline as energy. The Implicator's stress test shows this is the highest-risk sleeve per dollar.
BTC/USD.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an exchange failure or adverse regulatory action appears in the news.
